_comment: Provenance for the `verification` tier declared on each platform in
src/verticals/<vertical>/platforms/metadata.ts.
The metadata field says WHICH rung an adapter sits on. This file says who put
it there, when, and on what evidence — the same split `readScopes` has with
read-scopes-audit.json. Keeping the prose here is what stops 1,545-entry
catalog files turning into an audit log.
Every platform carrying a `verification` field MUST have an entry here, and
every entry here MUST name a platform that carries one. check:adapter-verification
fails on either mismatch, so the badge can never outlive its justification.
tier values (see packages/shared/src/reference/platform-verification.ts):
unit-tested  — transform + factory tests present and passing
verified     — OUR adapter driven against the platform's API: its sandbox
or test mode, or a live tenant
Sandbox and live tenant are one rung because a platform's sandbox serves the
same API as its production. Say which one the run used in `evidence`. Until
2026-11 they were two tiers, sandbox-verified and production-verified.
The distinction that matters: calling a platform's own API by hand proves the
PLATFORM works. verified means the request went through this repo's
adapter — its auth, its client, its transforms. Only the latter is a claim
about our code, and only the latter earns the rung.
`verifiedAt` is THE DATE THE EVIDENCE WAS PRODUCED — when the sync job ran, not
when this entry was typed up. check:adapter-verification compares it against the
adapter directory's last commit and warns when the code has moved on since, which
is the mechanism that stops a badge quietly becoming a lie.
The run date is load-bearing, and using the write-up date defeats the check: if
you run a sync on the 10th, the adapter changes on the 15th, and you record it on
the 16th, a write-up date hides the intervening commit and the warning never
fires. That happened on the first six entries and is why this now says so
explicitly. If the two dates differ, the run's date goes here; note the write-up
date in `evidence` if it matters.
To promote an adapter: do the work, then add or amend its entry here and set
the matching `verification` field in the vertical's metadata.ts. See
CONTRIBUTING.md § Adapter verification.

accounting/bokio.evidence: Driven through the integration-server against a Bokio company on api.bokio.se, via the adapter's own OAuth, client and transforms. Sync job feb42dd1 (2026-11-16) completed 1,254 rows across every resource the adapter implements: accounts 1242, bills 5, contacts 3, journals 3, invoices 1, creditmemos 0. The other six resources (transactions, taxrates, expenses, orders, salesorders, purchaseorders) are skipped by design because Bokio's API has no endpoint for them, and the job records each reason. An earlier run that day (a1936bfa) failed on accounts after 800 rows with 'Upstream platform unreachable: socket hang up', a network drop rather than an adapter error; the next run completed. Whether the Bokio company is a test company or a live one is not recorded here.

inventory/megaventory.evidence: Rebuilt from a Cin7 Core byte-clone — the file header still read "Cin7 Core adapter — reference implementation for the inventory vertical", it sent Cin7 paths (productList, ref/stockonhand, supplierList, purchaseList) to Megaventory host, and authenticated with a Bearer header Megaventory does not read. Megaventory publishes no readable documentation (megaventory.com/developers points at api.megaventory.com, which renders no content), so the adapter was written against the LIVE service own ServiceStack metadata on 2026-09-18: https://api.megaventory.com/v2017a/metadata lists all 112 operations and https://api.megaventory.com/v2017a/json/metadata?op=<Op> gives each request/response DTO. Every operation name was additionally probed against the live endpoint to confirm it resolves. NOT verified: no Megaventory account exists to drive our own client, auth and transforms through — API access requires a paid plan. The live probing corrected four things: errors are returned IN-BAND on HTTP 200 with ResponseStatus.ErrorCode, so an invalid key read as a successful empty sync; there is no pagination of any kind (ReturnTopNRecords is a top-N limiter ordered by id descending); dates are .NET format with DateTime.MinValue as the unset sentinel; and SupplierClientGet returns customers alongside suppliers. Stock-transfer and stock-adjustment have no operation at all — nine candidate names were probed and none resolves.

inventory/shipbob-inventory.evidence: Driven through the integration-server against the ShipBob sandbox (sandbox-api.shipbob.com) via the adapter own credential handling, client and transforms. Sync job 380e99bb (2026-09-18) completed 147 rows across all four implemented resources — stock-levels 84, products 38, purchase-orders 17, locations 8 — with suppliers, stock-transfers and stock-adjustments skipped, which is correct: metadata.ts declares all three unavailable because ShipBob has no such endpoint. Referential integrity was checked on the synced data: the location ids the stock levels reference (7, 9, 10, 80, 81, 82, 83, 85) are exactly the locations the sync returned, with no dangling reference. The run confirmed the rebuild end to end, including the oz-to-gram and inch-to-centimetre conversions (2722 g, 30.48 cm), the composite per-location stock id (16160673:80) and the Completed-to-received WRO mapping with 240 received against 120 ordered. Two defects were found by the live run and fixed before this entry: listStockLevels forwarded the caller limit as a PageSize of vendor ITEMS and then flattened each into per-location rows, so a request for 3 returned 19 and the router logged that it had truncated the response; and locations read GET /location, which is the only route here requiring the locations_read scope and which 401d with an empty body on a token carrying products_read, inventory_read and receiving_read. The location fix was to change endpoint rather than request the extra scope — GET /fulfillment-center returns the 8 centres this merchant uses rather than the 69-centre network of which 65 are access_granted false, needs no additional scope, and is what makes every stockLevel.locationId resolve.
